title: Parag Milk Foods Ltd - 539889 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q4 FY26: gross margin rose to 28% from 25.9% in Q3, but EBITDA margin slipped to about 8.1% and core-category volumes fell 3%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue crossed INR3,800 crores with 5% volume growth, and the new-age business (Avvatar and Pride of Cows) grew 91% for the year. Q4 gross margin improved to 28% (25.9% in Q3, 26.7% a year earlier) on mix and pricing, but employee costs jumped on one-offs and EBITDA margin dipped to about 8.1%. Q4 branded volumes fell about 5% and core-category volumes about 3%, which management attributed to a weak export and institutional base effect. Management guided only qualitatively: double-digit core volume growth as the aspiration, and a move to double-digit EBITDA margin over coming years.

financial_highlights.metric: New-age business revenue (Avvatar + Pride of Cows)
financial_highlights.value: over INR100 crores in Q4 (second straight quarter); about INR360 crores base cited by analyst
financial_highlights.change: over 100% YoY in Q4; 91% for FY26
vs 25.9% in Q3 FY26; 26.7% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: down about 5% YoY (core categories down about 3%)
about INR9 crores increase, from INR6 crores to about INR15 crores

financial_highlights.change: up about INR150 crores, attributed to rate variance (management says quantity variance nil)

segments.name: Core categories (Ghee, Cheese, Paneer)
segments.commentary: About 60% of business. Q4 volume down about 3%, due to lower export and institutional sales in the base quarter; YTD December volume growth was 12%. Management says Ghee is number 1 with about 22% market share; cheese about 35%.

segments.name: New-age (Avvatar, Pride of Cows)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores quarterly revenue for the second quarter running (INR102 crores prior quarter, INR100 crores in Q4), with revenue growing over 100% YoY in Q4. Pricing and promotion changes in Q4 created a transitional gap. Pride of Cows price raised from INR120 to INR135 per litre.

segments.name: Avvatar protein / sports nutrition
segments.commentary: Management estimates a 14-15% share of the protein segment on quick commerce and marketplaces only. About 65% of Avvatar sales come via e-commerce, per an analyst.

guidance_outlook: New-age share of revenue targeted at 20-25% in 3-5 years; management equates this to about INR1,000 crores within the INR10,000 crores ambition, but declined to give a FY29 number.
Capex guidance for FY27 of INR60-70 crores (FY26 spend about INR100 crores).
Aspiration of double-digit core-category volume growth; no formal FY27 guidance given.
Aspiration to move EBITDA margin to double digits in coming years (FY26 about 8.1%).
Gross margin expected to hold around 27-28%, subject to commodity inflation.
Milk prices expected to stay around INR42/litre for the next 2-3 months, then possibly soften after the monsoon if energy prices stay stable.
Full-year incentive income to fall marginally further from INR46 crores; quarterly sustainable employee cost about INR45-46 crores less about INR7.5-8 crores exceptional items.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to rise from 60 to 80 metric tons, then aiming for 120 metric tons through adjacency capex, not greenfield. Combined ghee and cheese capacity cited at about 110 metric tons.
Capex in FY26 about INR100 crores, mainly cheese expansion and lactose-to-whey improvement; some longer-gestation projects still pending.
Cold chain, warehousing and supply chain in North and South India described as already in place.
Dubai subsidiary: bank account opened in Q4 FY26, but first ODI not yet made; company-owned depot on hold for 2-3 months due to Middle East conflict.
demand_pricing: Q4 price increases taken on Ghee, liquid milk, Pride of Cows and Avvatar; management says gross profit growth has outpaced volume growth, indicating pricing power.
Management attributes the core volume decline to export and institutional sales in the base quarter and says ghee premium is intact.
Milk price inflation of 15% YoY passed on in a calibrated way; packaging cost up on polymer price inflation, which led to milk pouch price increases.
Q3 gross margin was hit by GST-driven price reductions (GST on core categories cut from 12% to 5%).
Whey prices rose sharply; management says whey pricing is driven by milk price volatility rather than global protein prices.
Management claims about 30,000 new general-trade outlets added every quarter, and aims to double SKU depth in existing outlets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the New-age business growth aspirations, and is a separate listing or valuation carve-out of Avvatar being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% of revenue from new-age in 3-5 years, but says it has never considered carving out Avvatar, citing an integrated farm-to-brand model.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new-age revenue been flat QoQ at about INR100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 saw promotions withdrawn on Pride of Cows, a price transition on Avvatar and a channel change, which created a transitional gap. Management expects growth from the INR100 crores base without giving a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 employee cost jump and the sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: One-offs included about INR9 crores of higher executive director pay (from INR6 crores to about INR15 crores), about INR5 crores of ESOP costs, appraisals and new business heads. Management said about INR7.5-8 crores are exceptional, leaving a regular quarterly run rate of about INR45-46 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core volume growth fall so sharply in Q4 and is there market share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Q4 branded volume fell about 5% and core about 3%, due to a low export base; it denied share loss and reiterated double-digit core volume growth as the aspiration.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin gains flow through to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sequential gross margin rose from about 26% when milk was INR40 to 28% at INR42, and expects to reach double-digit EBITDA over coming years, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the INR730 crore inventory increase?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crores of the increase is rate variance from inflation; quantity variance is nil, and powder inventory is expected to fall as that business shrinks.

risks_watch: Core-category volume trend: Q4 core volume down 3%, and management's double-digit core growth target has not yet been shown in results.
EBITDA margin compression (about 8.1%) despite gross margin gains; employee cost growth above 20% YoY.
Milk and energy price inflation, El Nino and fuel-driven packaging and logistics cost increases; management expects milk to stay at INR42 for 2-3 months.
Lower incentive income (INR46 crores vs INR88 crores) reduces other income support.
Inventory at about INR730 crores, with a rate-driven increase of about INR150 crores.
New-age momentum: Q4 flat QoQ at about INR100 crores; Avvatar e-commerce dependence (about 65%).
Middle East disruption delaying the Dubai depot and international expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and gross margin, but defensive on volume and EBITDA. Management attributed the core volume decline to base-period export and institutional sales, and left FY27 guidance qualitative. Several employee cost and inventory answers were given in a piecemeal way, which left some numbers unclear.
key_quotes: This was not driven by external factors, but by sharper execution.
we are fairly confident that we will inch up to double-digit margins.
We may not need a greenfield expansion when we have to increase the capacity from, say, 60 to overall 120, it can be done with the adjacency in the capex.

adds.what: Cheese capacity expansion from 60 to 80 metric tons (then targeting 120 MT via adjacency capex)

growth.why: Management gives no formal FY27 revenue guidance, only aspirations of double-digit core volume growth and a 20-25% new-age revenue share in 3-5 years; FY27 capex of INR60-70 crore and a cheese capacity rise from 60 to 80 MT are the only concrete items, with Q4 core volumes down about 3% and EBITDA margin about 8.1%.
